thread:
morgan: Heads up — last night's paid social campaign caused the rerank realtime pool to saturate around 23:10 UTC. p95 latencies spiked and we dropped a few low-priority requests :fire:
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-util=98% on rerank-pool-us-west-2. evicted 12 pods. timeline: 23:09-23:35 UTC.
keith: Oof. Did the batch backfill start during the window?
morgan: yep. Our nightly backfill kicked at 23:00 by infra-scheduler. It overlaps with the peak from the campaign. Rough numbers from logs: realtime peak 14k rps (small calls), most are 1-3 tokens rerank. Backfill consumed ~18 GPU-hours in that 1.5h window due to large batches (sequence len ~512).
anya: Can you paste the quick projection numbers? I want to be concrete for infra spend modeling.
morgan: quick paste — projections we ran locally:
```
Current steady: 6 GPUs in rerank-us-west (A100).
Peak observed: 10 GPUs needed to keep p95 < 200ms during campaign spikes.
Backfill job: 18 GPU-hours if runs unconstrained between 23:00-01:00.
If we move backfill to off-peak window (02:00-06:00) -> still 18 GPU-hours but lower overlap risk.
If we split batch into smaller shards + spot -> 8-10 GPU-hours of on-demand equivalent.
```
keith: So short-term options: 1) Move backfill window, 2) Split batch to dedicated batch pool (spot-friendly), 3) Autoscale realtime pool more aggressively, 4) Throttle non-critical customers during campaign spikes. Which is fastest?
sam: Moving backfill window is the lowest effort. We can change scheduler cron and add a guard that prevents batch from starting if gpu-util > 75%. infra-scheduler-bot can support that check.
infra-scheduler-bot: SCHEDULER PROPOSAL: add preconditions to nightly-backfill job: `if rerank-pool-gpu-util > 0.75 then delay 30m (max 4 retries)` — will open PR.
anya: Good. But for predictable capacity planning (Q2 campaigns) we should model seasonal demand. Data point: we expect two more similar campaigns in April and June. If each needs 4 extra GPUs for 3h -> ~72 GPU-hours across two regions. That changes our reserved vs spot math.
tina: Region constraint: eu-west capacity is thin this month; we can't easily spin +4 A100s there. US-West has more headroom. Maybe route EU campaign traffic to US when latency delta is acceptable?\e.g., consider policy: route-eu-to-us for non-authenticated rerank (500ms target) and keep eu-only for auth flows.
keith: Cost note: On-demand A100 = X, spot ~0.4X but preempt risk. For forecasting, assume 60% spot availability — so plan 0.6 * spot_hours + 0.4 * on-demand as blended. We'll produce two scenarios: optimistic (mostly spot) and conservative (mostly on-demand/reserved).
morgan: For immediate mitigation I'm proposing: change backfill window to 02:30, add scheduler precondition, and create a temporary small batch-only pool (min 2 GPUs spot, max 6) in us-west for the next 3 weeks.
sam: I can deploy the scheduler change today and spin the batch pool in us-west as spot nodes. Will monitor preemptions.
keith: I'll run a short capacity simulation to estimate throughput and p95 under the above config and post numbers by EOD. I'll include GPU-hours and cost deltas for both spot-heavy and reserved options.
anya: Also add a metric for "fraction of batch overlap with peak" to the weekly capacity dashboard. We need the number to be <5% for acceptable SLO burn.
morgan: Action items: sam -> update cron + batch pool (today). keith -> sim + cost scenarios (EOD). anya -> update capacity dashboard (this week). Tina -> check EU routing/legal constraints for routing EU traffic to US.
keith: quick command I'll use for the sim:
```bash
python tools/capacity_sim.py --workload rerank --peak 14000 --batch_hours 18 --regions us-west,eu-west --spot_fraction 0.6
```
morgan: sounds good. If we still see saturation after these changes, we'll consider temporarily increasing dedicated capacity for 2 weeks (budget ask).
sam: starting work now. Will ping when precondition PR is up.
keith: thanks, all. ping @morgan if you want me to include a recommended reserved commit for Q2 in the simulation. :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: we'll keep an eye on evictions metric and alert if >5 evictions/6h.
morgan: closing loop — appreciate the quick responses.
keith: ack.
